text: To construct a square equal to a given rectilinear figure. Let $A$ be the given rectilinear figure. So it is required to construct a square equal to the rectilinear figure $A$.
For let the right-angled parallelogram $BD$, equal to the rectilinear figure $A$, be constructed [Prop. 1.45].
Therefore, if $BE$ is equal to $ED$ then that (which) was prescribed has taken place.
assertion: if BE = ED then the square BD is the answer

text: For the square $BD$, equal to the rectilinear figure $A$, has been constructed.
assertion: square BD equals rectilinear figure A

text: And if not, (then) one of the (straight-lines) $BE$ or $ED$ is greater (than the other).
assertion: if BE ≠ ED then one is greater

text: Let $BE$ be greater, and let it be produced to $F$,
and let $EF$ be made equal to $ED$ [Prop.~1.3].
And let $BF$ be cut in half at (point) $G$ [Prop.~1.10].
And, with center $G$, and radius one of the (straight-lines) $GB$ or $GF$, let the semi-circle $BHF$ be drawn.
And let $DE$ be produced to $H$,
and let $GH$ be joined.

Therefore, since the straight-line $BF$ has been cut---equally at $G$, and unequally at $E$---the rectangle contained by $BE$ and $EF$, plus the square on $EG$, is thus equal to the square on $GF$ [Prop.~2.5].
assertion: rectangle BE*EF + square EG = square GF

justifications.substring: the straight-line $BF$ has been cut---equally at $G$, and unequally at $E$

text: And $GF$ (is) equal to $GH$.
Thus, the (rectangle contained) by $BE$ and $EF$, plus the (square) on $GE$, is equal to the (square) on $GH$.
assertion: rectangle BE*EF + square GE = square GH

text: And the (sum of the) squares on $HE$ and $EG$ is equal to the (square) on $GH$ [Prop.~1.47].
assertion: square HE + square EG = square GH

text: Thus, the (rectangle contained) by $BE$ and $EF$, plus the (square) on $GE$, is equal to the (sum of the squares) on $HE$ and $EG$.
assertion: rectangle BE*EF + square GE = square HE + square EG

text: Let the square on $GE$ be taken from both.
assertion: subtract square GE from both sides

text: Thus, the remaining rectangle contained by $BE$ and $EF$ is equal to the square on $EH$.
But, $BD$ is the (rectangle contained) by $BE$ and $EF$. For $EF$ (is) equal to $ED$.
assertion: BD is the rectangle contained by BE and EF

text: Thus, the parallelogram $BD$ is equal to the square on $HE$.
And $BD$ (is) equal to the rectilinear figure $A$.
Thus, the rectilinear figure $A$ is also equal to the square (which) can be described on $EH$.
assertion: rectilinear figure A = square on EH

text: Thus, a square---(namely), that (which) can be described on $EH$---has been constructed, equal to the given rectilinear figure $A$. (Which is) the very thing it was required to do.
